title: The Decomposition Paradox
description: More decomposition HURTS raw LLMs but HELPS fine-tuned ones. D-R-H-F on raw ChatGPT: F1=1.81 (worst). With QLoRA: F1=53.01 (best). Implication: for few-shot extraction without fine-tuning, use LESS decomposition. For fine-tuned pipelines, use MORE decomposition.
implications_for_few_shot: When designing few-shot examples for Haiku/Sonnet extraction (no fine-tuning), prefer D-F or D-RS-F patterns over D-R-H-F. The full RHF decomposition requires fine-tuning to overcome error accumulation.

title: Relation Descriptions are Highest-Leverage Intervention
description: Rewriting Wikidata descriptions with examples improved F1 from 6.44 to 14.04 (+118%). This is a larger effect than model choice or paradigm choice. Implication: invest in clear, example-rich relation type definitions before scaling extraction.
implications_for_few_shot: Every few-shot example MUST include clear relation type definitions with concrete examples. This is more important than the number of few-shot examples.

title: Error Accumulation in Sequential Pipelines
description: AutoRE individual module performance: Relation F1=72, Head F1=74, Fact F1=84. But end-to-end AutoRE F1=53. The ~20 point gap is pure error accumulation through the pipeline. Each module's errors compound.
implications_for_few_shot: For few-shot extraction, minimize pipeline steps. If using multi-step, each step must be HIGH precision even at cost of recall. Better to miss relations than to hallucinate them.

title: ChatGPT Fails at Document-Level RE
description: All 4 paradigms on raw ChatGPT yield F1 < 8%. ChatGPT 'does not adequately comprehend subject-object relationships in RE tasks'. BERT-based models outperform ChatGPT on Standard-IE. LLMs need fine-tuning OR structured decomposition+guidance for RE.
implications_for_few_shot: Raw LLM extraction without few-shot OR fine-tuning is nearly useless for structured RE. This explains Haiku's 50x variance in our Phase 1 experiment — without structured examples, each agent invented its own (bad) approach.
